question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: input is not a map (none, a list, text, a number or a bool) -> throws. Entries other than sirFiles and variants are ignored.
FILES = the entry sirFiles: missing -> the empty list; a list -> its elements; anything else (none included) -> throws. An element that is not text -> throws.

CLAIM-OF(path) is an id, nothing, or a throw. BASE = the part of path after its last "/" or "\" (all of path when it holds neither), with SPACE-TAB characters removed from both ends (only those). A SIR-END is the four characters "." then one of SIR-CASE's s S, one of i I, one of r R — an ASCII-only fold. (a) BASE is text that ends with a SIR-END, followed by one or more HIDDEN characters to the very end -> throws. (b) Otherwise, BASE not ending with a SIR-END -> nothing (x.ts.sir.bak, x.ts.sir~, x.ts.sir/, README.md, x.ts.ſir, x.ts.sır). (c) Otherwise STEM = BASE without its last four characters, cut at every "." into SEGMENTS; UNIT = the first SEGMENT. UNIT not empty and not a UNIT-NAME -> throws (x y.ts.sir, é.sir, -x.ts.sir, a<LF>b.rust.sir; an empty UNIT is allowed). More than two SEGMENTS -> throws (a.b.ts.sir, x.go.ts.sir, ...sir). One SEGMENT -> nothing (x.sir, .sir, ts.sir). Two: the second empty -> throws (x..sir, ..sir); else the claim is the second exactly as written, no case change or trim (.php.sir claims php; a.b.sir claims b, which R4 refuses).
SIGHT(id): id not in REGISTRY (exact, case-sensitive) -> throws; otherwise id is SIGHTED. Each element of FILES with a claim is sighted: x.TS.sir, x.carried.sir and "x. ts.sir" throw.

VARIANTS = the entry variants: missing or none -> no entries; a map -> its entries; anything else (a list, text, number or bool — false and 0 included) -> throws. Entry order is immaterial: every check below is per entry or over all entries.

For each entry K -> V of VARIANTS: (a) V not a map -> throws. V has an entry lang that is not text (none included) -> throws. V has an entry sir that is not text -> throws. V has a text sir: CLAIM-OF(sir) is taken (it may throw, R3), and BASE of sir (as R3 cuts it) not ending with a SIR-END -> throws (the empty text, "/", README.md, x.ts.sir.bak, x.ts.sir/). (b) K is neither exactly package nor exactly lang: followed by a LANG-ID -> throws (Lang:ts, lang:, lang:TS, lang:1ts, " lang:ts", default, look-alikes with a Cyrillic letter, a fullwidth colon or an invisible character). The LANG-ID runs to the very end of K: lang:ts followed by a line feed throws. (c) KEYLANG = the LANG-ID of a lang: key (none for package); OWNLANG = V's lang (the empty text included); PATHLANG = CLAIM-OF(V's sir) when V has a sir. NAMED = those present. (d) two members of NAMED differ (exact comparison) -> throws. (e) KEYLANG or OWNLANG present, V has a sir, and PATHLANG is nothing -> throws (lang:ts, or package with lang ts, and sir x.sir). (f) NAMED empty -> the entry contributes nothing (only a package key without lang whose sir is absent or a one-SEGMENT name). (g) otherwise SIGHT(the one id NAMED holds) — so lang:go or an empty lang throws — and that id is claimed by K: two entries claiming one id -> throws. A FILES claim and a variant claim of the same id do not conflict.
The result is the SIGHTED ids, each once, in ascending order (every REGISTRY id is ASCII lowercase, so any text order agrees). A throw anywhere is the outcome of the whole call: no partial result.
